To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the common Ile399Thr and–118T>10 polymorphs of UDP-glucuronosytransferase 1a9 (UGTIA9) do not explain inter-individual variability in the glucoronidation of xenobiotes in the human liver, because they do not correlate with either the activity or the mRNA expression of the UGTIA9 protein.
the common I39SC>T and–1189T>T polymorphisms in UGTTA9 do not explain inter-individual variation in hepatic activity or mRNA expression of UGT1A.
we have found no evidence that the common UGT1A1 polymorphisms I399C>T or–118T9>T affect the activity of UGT1A6 or UGT1A7.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the genetic polymorphisms of the UGT 1A family of enzymes and its effect on the pharmacokinetics of the drug Flavopiridol.
the study of the relationship between genetic polymorphisms and the activity of the enzyme UDP-glucuronide transferase (UGT).
the development of a new class of compounds for the treatment of chronic hepatitis B virus infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the common UGT1A1 and UGT1B1 variants, but not the common UGTs 1A7, 1A9, 1A10, 2B15, and 2B17, are functionally important.

the common UGT1A1 and UGT1B1 polymorphisms are associated with interindividual variability in UGT1B7 and UGT1As, respectively, but the common UGT2B7 and UCT1A9 variants are not associated with interindividual variation in their corresponding enzymes.
common UGT1A7 and UGT1B1 polymorphisms are responsible for the observed variability in UGT1 family activity, and that common UGT2B15 polymorphisms are not.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
common variants in UGT1 are not associated with UGT1A activity and mRNA expression.
common variants in UGT1a9 do not appear to be functionally significant in the livers we studied.
the common polymorphisms in UG1A9 do not explain the interindividual variability in glucuronidation activity.

the common UGT1A8 polymorphisms do NOT explain the interindividual variability in the hepatic glucuronidation activity of UGT1A1, 1A3, and 1A4 substrates.
